    Stripe Setup Guide

    This guide covers Stripe configuration for different environments. Follow the section that matches your setup.

    Table of Contents

    • Step 1: Get API Keys
    • Step 2: Create Products and Get Price IDs
    • Step 3: Set Up Webhooks (CRITICAL)
    • Scenario 1: Local Development (Test Mode)
    • Scenario 2: VPS Testing (Test Mode)
    • Scenario 3: VPS Production (Live Mode)
    • Step 4: Customer Portal Settings
    • Step 5: Set Up Test Clock (Optional)

    Step 1: Get API Keys

    1. Log in to your Stripe Dashboard: https://dashboard.stripe.com
    2. Navigate to Developers → API keys

    3. Copy the following keys:

      For Test Mode (development/testing): - Publishable key (pk_test_...) - Secret key (sk_test_...)

      For Live Mode (production): - Publishable key (pk_live_...) - Secret key (sk_live_...)

    4. Add these to your .env file: env STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_...

    Step 2: Create Products and Get Price IDs

    You need to create products in both Test Mode and Live Mode separately.

    Creating Products

    1. Go to Product catalog → Add product
    2. Create the Pro Plan:
      • Name: Pro Plan
      • Pricing: Recurring, Monthly
      • Amount: (e.g., $25.00)
      • Click Save product
    3. Create the Pro Plus Plan:
      • Name: Pro Plus Plan
      • Pricing: Recurring, Monthly
      • Amount: (e.g., $99.00)
      • Click Save product

    Getting Price IDs

    1. Open each product you just created
    2. In the Pricing section, copy the API ID (starts with price_...)

    3. Add these to your .env file:

      Test Mode: env STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID=price_1XXX... VITE_STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID=price_1XXX... STRIPE_PRO_PLUS_PRICE_ID=price_1YYY... VITE_STRIPE_PRO_PLUS_PRICE_ID=price_1YYY...

      Live Mode (for production): ```env

      PRODUCTION:STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID=price_1ZZZ...

      PRODUCTION:VITE_STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID=price_1ZZZ...

      PRODUCTION:STRIPE_PRO_PLUS_PRICE_ID=price_1AAA...

      PRODUCTION:VITE_STRIPE_PRO_PLUS_PRICE_ID=price_1AAA...

      ```

    Page top-ups (one-time prices)

    Top-up billing uses four packs ($2, $5, $10, $15). Stripe charges the pack amount; your app credits pages using:

    pages = round(top_up_amount_usd ÷ price_per_page_usd)

    Default per-page rates (change anytime in .env without touching Stripe):

    Top-up Default $/page Pages credited (default)
    $2 $0.35 6
    $5 $0.30 17
    $10 $0.20 50
    $15 $0.15 100

    Option A — Automated setup (recommended)

    From the repo root, with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in .env (test or live key):

    python scripts/setup_stripe_api_topups.py --write-env

    This calls the Stripe API to:

    1. Create one Product named Nolain API Page Top-ups (a container in Stripe for related prices).
    2. Create four Prices on that product — one-time charges of $2, $5, $10, and $15 (not subscriptions).
    3. Append the Price IDs and default per-page rates to .env.

    Restart the backend after updating .env.

    Option B — Stripe Dashboard (manual)

    Do this at dashboard.stripe.com in Test mode (toggle top-right) while developing.

    1. Create the product (container)

    1. Go to Product catalog → Products → + Add product.
    2. Name: Nolain API Page Top-ups.
    3. Description (optional): prepaid API page credits.
    4. Leave pricing empty on this screen — you will add prices next.
    5. Save. Open the product and copy the Product ID (prod_...) if needed for reference.

    2. Add four one-time prices

    For each amount ($2, $5, $10, $15):

    1. On the product page, click Add another price (or Add price).
    2. Pricing model: Standard pricing.
    3. Price: enter 2.00 / 5.00 / 10.00 / 15.00 USD.
    4. Billing period: choose One time (not monthly/yearly — that would be a subscription).
    5. Save.
    6. Copy the Price ID (price_...) from the price row.

    3. Wire Price IDs into the app

    STRIPE_API_TOPUP_2_PRICE_ID=price_...
STRIPE_API_TOPUP_5_PRICE_ID=price_...
STRIPE_API_TOPUP_10_PRICE_ID=price_...
STRIPE_API_TOPUP_15_PRICE_ID=price_...

# Per-page rates — adjust later without new Stripe prices:
API_TOPUP_2_PRICE_PER_PAGE=0.35
API_TOPUP_5_PRICE_PER_PAGE=0.30
API_TOPUP_10_PRICE_PER_PAGE=0.20
API_TOPUP_15_PRICE_PER_PAGE=0.15

    Repeat in Live mode with live keys when you go to production.

    Supabase

    Run SQL migrations: backend/sql/add_api_billing_columns.sql, create_api_credit_purchases_table.sql.

    If upgrading from the legacy API billing schema, also run backend/sql/migrate_api_billing_to_topup.sql.

    Rules

    • Subscriptions and top-up credits can coexist. Top-up pages act as overflow beyond the monthly quota.
    • Webhooks must receive checkout.session.completed for top-up purchases.

    Step 3: Set Up Webhooks (CRITICAL)

    ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Webhook setup differs significantly based on your environment. Choose the correct scenario below.

    Scenario 1: Local Development (Test Mode)

    When to use: Running the app on your local machine via npm run dev or docker-compose and accessing it at http://localhost

    Setup Steps:

    1. Install Stripe CLI ```bash # On macOS brew install stripe/stripe-cli/stripe

      On Linux

      Download from: https://github.com/stripe/stripe-cli/releases

      ```

    2. Authenticate with Stripe bash stripe login

    3. Configure your local .env env FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost

    4. Start your application bash docker-compose up -d

    5. Run Stripe CLI listener (in a separate terminal) bash stripe listen --forward-to http://localhost:8000/webhook

      Note: If using Docker, the backend is accessible at localhost:8000 directly, or via nginx at localhost/api/webhook

    6. Copy the webhook signing secret

      The CLI will output something like: ```

      Ready! Your webhook signing secret is whsec_xxxxxxxxxxxxx (^C to quit) ```

      Copy that whsec_... value

    7. Update .env with the webhook secret env STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_xxxxxxxxxxxxx

    8. Restart backend to load new secret bash docker-compose restart backend

    9. Test the setup

      • Go to http://localhost in your browser
      • Click "Upgrade plan" and complete a test checkout (card: 4242 4242 4242 4242)
      • You should see webhook events appear in the Stripe CLI terminal
      • Check backend logs: docker-compose logs -f backend

    Scenario 2: VPS Testing (Test Mode)

    When to use: Running the app on a VPS and accessing it via a domain or IP address, but still testing with Stripe Test Mode

    ⚠️ CRITICAL: You CANNOT use Stripe CLI for this scenario. You must use Dashboard webhooks.

    Setup Steps:

    1. Configure VPS .env with your actual domain

      SSH into your VPS and edit .env: bash nano /path/to/project/.env

      Set: ```env FRONTEND_URL=https://yourdomain.com

      Or if not using SSL yet:

      FRONTEND_URL=http://your-vps-ip

      ```

    2. Create webhook endpoint in Stripe Dashboard

      a. Go to: https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/webhooks

      b. Click "Add endpoint"

      c. Endpoint URL: https://yourdomain.com/api/webhook (Or http://your-vps-ip/api/webhook if not using SSL)

      d. Click "Select events" and choose: - checkout.session.completed - customer.subscription.created - customer.subscription.updated - customer.subscription.deleted - invoice.payment_succeeded

      e. Click "Add endpoint"

      f. Copy the "Signing secret" (whsec_...)

    3. Update VPS .env with webhook secret bash nano /path/to/project/.env

      Set: env STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_xxxxxxxxxxxxx

    4. Restart Docker containers bash docker-compose down docker-compose up -d

    5. Test the setup

      • Go to your domain in browser
      • Click "Upgrade plan" and complete a test checkout (card: 4242 4242 4242 4242)
      • Check webhook events in Stripe Dashboard: https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/webhooks
      • Check backend logs: docker-compose logs -f backend

    ✅ Why this is different from local: - You're accessing via a public domain/IP, not localhost - Stripe's servers can reach your webhook endpoint directly - Stripe CLI cannot intercept webhooks for public domains - You must use Dashboard webhooks instead

    Scenario 3: VPS Production (Live Mode)

    When to use: Running the app on a VPS in production with real payments

    Setup Steps:

    1. Switch to Live Mode in Stripe Dashboard

      Toggle the "Test mode" switch in the top right to OFF

    2. Create webhook endpoint for Live Mode

      a. Go to: https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks (note: no /test/ in URL)

      b. Click "Add endpoint"

      c. Endpoint URL: https://yourdomain.com/api/webhook

      d. Click "Select events" and choose: - checkout.session.completed - customer.subscription.created - customer.subscription.updated - customer.subscription.deleted - invoice.payment_succeeded

      e. Click "Add endpoint"

      f. Copy the "Signing secret" (whsec_...)

      ⚠️ Note: This will be a DIFFERENT signing secret from test mode

    3. Update VPS .env with production values bash nano /path/to/project/.env

      Uncomment the production lines (remove the #PRODUCTION: prefix): ```env

      Use live mode keys

      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_... STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_live_... STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... # Live mode webhook secret STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID=price_... # Live mode price ID STRIPE_PRO_PLUS_PRICE_ID=price_... # Live mode price ID

      Frontend (do the same for VITE_ vars)

      VITE_STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID=price_... VITE_STRIPE_PRO_PLUS_PRICE_ID=price_...

      FRONTEND_URL=https://yourdomain.com ```

    4. Rebuild frontend with production values bash docker-compose down docker-compose up -d --build

      ⚠️ Important: Frontend environment variables are baked into the build, so you must rebuild

    5. Test with real card (be ready to refund)

      • Use a real credit card
      • Complete a subscription purchase
      • Immediately cancel and refund from Stripe Dashboard if this is just a test
      • Verify webhooks are received in Dashboard

    🔒 Security Notes: - Always use HTTPS in production (https:// not http://) - Keep your live API keys secure - Never commit live keys to git

    Step 4: Customer Portal Settings

    Configure how users manage their own subscriptions.

    1. Go to Settings (gear icon) → Billing → Customer portal
    2. Click Activate portal (if not already active)
    3. Under Subscription management:
      • Enable Cancel subscriptions
      • Enable Switch plans
      • Prorations: Enable "Prorate subscription changes" to charge/credit users immediately when they upgrade or downgrade
    4. Under Business information:
      • Add your Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs
    5. Click Save changes

    ⚠️ Note: Customer portal settings apply to both test and live mode. Configure it once and it works for both.

    Step 5: Set Up Test Clock (Optional)

    Test clocks allow you to simulate the passage of time to test subscription renewals and expirations.

    Only available in Test Mode.

    1. Go to Customers → Test clocks
    2. Click Create test clock
    3. Give it a name (e.g., "Monthly Renewal Test")
    4. When creating test customers: Associate them with this test clock
    5. Advance the clock: From the Stripe Dashboard to trigger renewal events
    6. Verify webhooks: Check that your webhook handler processes the events correctly

    Manual Supabase Updates (if needed)

    If webhooks haven't fired or you need to manually link test data:

    UPDATE subscriptions 
SET stripe_customer_id = 'cus_...', 
    stripe_subscription_id = 'sub_...' 
WHERE user_id = 'your_test_user_uuid';

    Common Issues & Troubleshooting

    "Invalid signature" webhook errors

    Cause: The STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in your .env doesn't match the webhook endpoint.

    Solutions: - Local: Make sure you copied the signing secret from the Stripe CLI output and restarted your backend - VPS: Make sure you copied the signing secret from the Dashboard webhook endpoint and restarted containers - After changes: Always restart: docker-compose restart backend

    Webhooks not received on VPS

    Cause: Using Stripe CLI when accessing via a public domain.

    Solution: Follow Scenario 2 or Scenario 3 and use Dashboard webhooks instead of CLI.

    Frontend shows wrong prices

    Cause: Frontend environment variables are baked into the build.

    Solution: After changing any VITE_* variables, rebuild:

    docker-compose down
docker-compose up -d --build

    FRONTEND_URL is still localhost

    Cause: Forgot to update FRONTEND_URL in VPS .env.

    Solution: Update .env with your actual domain and restart containers.

    Quick Reference

    Environment Access URL Webhook Method FRONTEND_URL Stripe Mode
    Local Dev http://localhost Stripe CLI http://localhost Test
    VPS Test https://yourdomain.com Dashboard https://yourdomain.com Test
    VPS Prod https://yourdomain.com Dashboard https://yourdomain.com Live
